pull.title: net: serve `MSG_BLOCK` by stripping witnesses in place
pull.body:
**Problem:** To send a `MSG_BLOCK` reply from disk, a node currently decodes the block and serializes it again without witnesses.
For `MSG_WITNESS_BLOCK`, it already sends the stored bytes directly.
Serving `MSG_BLOCK` efficiently also matters for the proposed witnessless initial block download. [#36476](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36476)

**Fix:** For `MSG_BLOCK` replies from disk on non-Signet chains, read the block into an owned byte buffer and check the header’s proof of work and expected hash.
Walk the serialized transactions directly and strip their witnesses in place.
Signet still uses `ReadBlock` to verify the Signet solution.
Header checks now run before transaction parsing, so if both the header and transaction data are corrupt, the node may log a different error.

**Performance:**
| Block | Before | After | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `block413567` | 3.204 ms | 0.369 ms | **8.7×** |
| Same block with synthetic witnesses | 8.944 ms | 1.026 ms | **8.7×** |

The synthetic fixture adds a 512-byte witness item and an empty item to every input.

**Related work:** This extends the path that sends witness blocks directly from disk. [#13151](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/13151)
Earlier work identified unnecessary transaction hashing when serving historical blocks. [#13011 discussion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/13011#issuecomment-383145046) · [#13098](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/13098)
The implementation also builds on bulk block reads. [#31551](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31551)

tACK 0b01ce05e162ee61fb0e3c0d8413e0e1af4c1976

I checked that the new `MSG_BLOCK` reply is byte for byte the old one. On 214 blocks, the head's `ReadBlockWithoutWitness` matches its `ReadBlock` plus `TX_NO_WITNESS`, that old path matches the base's, and btclib, a library I maintain, agrees. The blocks are mainnet 481824, 709632, 774628, 920000 and the bench's 413567, plus 209 regtest blocks with segwit v0 and v1 spends, 1,000 witness items, empty stacks and items, a 3,990,000-byte annex, 300 inputs, 316 outputs, 260 transactions, or no witness. Over P2P, a head node and a base node give the same `MSG_BLOCK` and `MSG_WITNESS_BLOCK` payloads for all 209: 208 from disk, and the two successive tips from the recent-block cache.

Each of seven mutants of `StripBlockWitness` and `ReadBlockWithoutWitness` fails `blockmanager_tests`. They range from keeping the marker or the witnesses to skipping the proof-of-work or hash check. The new `p2p_getdata` case also passes against a base node, so it guards the payload format rather than the new path.

Building the reply got 7.2x to 9.0x faster than on the base for those five mainnet blocks and the two largest regtest blocks (median of three runs, Release, Apple M5). Peak heap fell from 2.9 to 2.0 MB for 481824 and from 7.9 to 4.0 MB for 774628. I measured with a Boost test that writes each block with `WriteBlock` and reads it back both ways, and a functional test running a head and a base node; I can share both as a gist.

tACK d36943b49ce321cd622a8ae5a885227c7b3189cf

The PR's own changes are the ones I tested on 0b01ce05: the range-diff only moves three bench includes into the earlier bench commits and places the new tests before master's new `blockmanager_tests` case, and the net diff is unchanged line for line. The new base widens block file positions to 64 bits, which the new read path goes through, so I re-ran the byte-for-byte check rather than carry the old result over.

On this head, `ReadBlockWithoutWitness` matches `ReadBlock` plus `TX_NO_WITNESS` for the same five mainnet blocks and for 263 new regtest blocks, and btclib agrees. The regtest blocks include taproot annexes of up to 3,990,001 bytes, witness stacks of 1,001 items, 260 transactions, 300 inputs and 316 outputs, and three blocks with no witness. Over P2P, `MSG_BLOCK` equals the test framework's non-witness serialization for all 263 blocks read from disk and for 22 of them while they were the tip. `MSG_WITNESS_BLOCK` equals `getblock`. `blockmanager_tests`, `p2p_getdata`, `p2p_segwit` and `p2p_compactblocks` pass. I did not re-run the mutants or the timings. Scripts and output: https://gist.github.com/fametrano/740bc1f88f3d5967023c920824bafd70/29865a5e048c740b1ac50fbc311e2f1607bfaa3d
Rebased + applied some minor Fable 5.2 simplification suggestions.
